cond_0001.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0001.requirements:
Education:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements:
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, a capacity to be self-motivated and work independently.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0024.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are looking for a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. Both centers are premier research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member working alongside other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will regularly train new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations, operate instruments on behalf of users, and actively represent the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity to work hands-on with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0024.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Regularly connects with team members to collect data and monitor test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Actively participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials, contributing ideas and raising questions in team discussions
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0024.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences, including an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to train or teach effectively and work collaboratively with users and team members on a regular basis
Preferred Requirements
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study
Good organizational skills and ability to work independently

cond_0070.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are seeking a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support operations of expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, and private industry. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
The Cryo-EM Research Specialist will work alongside other center scientists, with responsibilities covering user training on sample preparation and instrument operations, instrument operation on behalf of users, and representing the centers at meetings, conferences, and exhibits within the local [Location masked] and broader research community. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art facilities.
We are looking for a candidate with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience, though team training across cryo-EM modalities is available.

Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0070.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, and an ability to work independently.
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are looking for a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. Both centers are premier research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member working alongside other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will regularly train new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations, operate instruments on behalf of users, and actively represent the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity to work hands-on with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0078.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Regularly connects with team members to collect data and monitor test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Actively participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials, contributing ideas and raising questions in team discussions
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0078.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences, including an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to train or teach effectively and work collaboratively with users and team members on a regular basis
Preferred Requirements
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study
Good organizational skills and ability to work independently

cond_0113.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked]. Most people become stronger in this kind of microscopy and sample preparation work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0113.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0113.requirements:
Education:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements:
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, a capacity to be self-motivated and work independently.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0121.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked]. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of cryo-EM instrumentation and sample preparation workflows.

Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.

25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders

10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0121.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, a capacity to be self-motivated and work independently.
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0129.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0129.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0129.requirements:
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum Requirements:
Around 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences, which could include exposure to cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline — or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Some experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Ability to communicate effectively, work collaboratively, and stay organized; willingness to train or teach others and to work independently when needed.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Background in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Familiarity with correlating images or data from multiple instruments to target a region of interest or enhance the overall analysis of a sample.

cond_0153.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are looking to bring on a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to help support our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. Both centers are premier research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
Working alongside other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will help train new users, assist with instrument operations, and represent the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position offers a genuine opportunity to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to help support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0153.responsibilities:
40% Coordinates with center scientists to conduct research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Works with the team to track inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates collaboratively in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0153.requirements:
Education:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements:
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, and a capacity to work independently.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0169.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are seeking a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support operations of expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. Both centers are research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, and private industry. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
The Cryo-EM Research Specialist will work alongside other center scientists, with responsibilities covering user training on sample preparation and instrument operations, operating instruments on behalf of users, and representing the centers at meetings, conferences, and exhibits within the local [Location masked] and broader research community. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art facilities.
We are looking for a candidate with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. There are also opportunities for team training across all cryo-EM modalities. This specialist will join a team of scientists supporting the growing cryo-EM research resources at [Location masked].

cond_0283.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked]. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of cryo-EM instrumentation and sample preparation workflows.

The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0317.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0317.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 2 years of demonstrated expertise in relevant research in the biological sciences, with a solid understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Deep knowledge of light microscopy including fluorescence, and proficiency in electron microscopy.
Strong command of microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, strong ability to collaborate effectively in a research setting, solid organizational skills, proven ability to train or teach effectively, and the capacity to work independently with minimal direction.
Expertise in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Proven track record in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest and enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].

cond_0350.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are seeking a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to take ownership of operations at our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are premier research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, and private industry. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
The Cryo-EM Research Specialist will lead training of new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations, execute instrument sessions on behalf of users, and represent the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position offers a strong opportunity to work directly with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to advance the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0350.responsibilities:
40% Leads and executes research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results.
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders.
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences.
10% Drives the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials.
5% Delivers operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers.
10% Conducts literature reviews and writes reports.
cond_0350.requirements:
Education:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
Minimum Requirements:
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences, including an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, and a capacity to work independently.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0374.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked]. Most people become stronger in this kind of microscopy work over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from working alongside the team.

The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are seeking a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to lead operations across our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are premier research facilities with missions to develop and make available advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, and private industry. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
In this role, you will take ownership of user training on sample preparation and instrument operations, execute instrument sessions on behalf of users, and represent the centers at meetings, conferences, and exhibits within the local [Location masked] and broader research community. This position offers a strong opportunity to work directly with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art facilities.
We are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. There are also ample opportunities for team training across all cryo-EM modalities. The successful candidate will join a team of scientists and help drive the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0467.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and executes one or more research projects and directs the daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Leads the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0467.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field
At least 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences that could include an understanding of cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline.
Experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy.
Experience with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, a talent for collaborative research, good organizational skills, an ability to train or teach effectively, a capacity to be self-motivated and work independently.
Experience in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Experience in correlating images or data from multiple instruments to both target a region of interest or enhance the total analysis of the sample under study.

cond_0483.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are looking to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, working closely with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will regularly train new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations, operate instruments on behalf of users, and actively represent the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. cond_0491.intro:
The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET seek to hire a Cryo-EM Research Specialist to support the operations of our expanding cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) facilities. These are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM Research Specialist will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked]. Most people become stronger in this kind of microscopy and sample preparation work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.

The [Company name masked] Cryo-EM Research Center and the NIH-funded Midwest Center for Cryo-ET are premier research facilities with missions to develop and to make available the advanced cryo-EM instrumentation and techniques for bioscience researchers from academia, government, or private industry laboratories. Instruments currently include two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, one 200 kV Talos Arctica TEM, one 120 kV Talos L120C TEM, two Aquilos 2+ cryo-FIB-SEMs, two Vitrobot plunge-freezers, Leica EM-GP2 plunge-freezer, CryoSol VitroJet, Leica Ice high-pressure freezer, Leica cryo-confocal CLEM system, cryo-ultramicrotome, Primo micropatterning system, optical microscopes, glow discharge, carbon-coating devices, and more.
As a team member, along with other center scientists, the Cryo-EM research specialist, will be responsible for training new center users on sample preparation and instrument operations; operating instruments on behalf of users; and representing the centers within the local [Location masked] and broader research community at meetings, conferences, and exhibits. This position is an excellent opportunity for an individual to work with cutting-edge instrumentation for cryo-EM, cryo-ET, micro-ED, and cryo-FIB milling in state-of-the-art cryo-EM research facilities.
Ideally, we are looking for a colleague with previous molecular biology, light microscopy, or electron microscopy experience. However, there are ample opportunities for team training in all cryo-EM modalities. This Cryo-EM Research Specialist will join a team of scientists to support the growing cryo-EM research resources and community at [Location masked].
cond_0516.responsibilities:
Develops, designs, and conducts one or more research projects and organizes daily operation of projects and specialized research areas to ensure work meets established objectives under moderate supervision.
40% Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
25% Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
10% Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
10% Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
5% Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers
10% Performs literature reviews and writes reports
cond_0516.requirements:
Education: Bachelor's degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Physics, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around 1 to 2 years of relevant research experience in the biological sciences, which could include exposure to cell biology, microbiology, protein biochemistry, or another appropriate sub-discipline. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
Some experience with light microscopy including fluorescence, and possibly electron microscopy — candidates still building this background are welcome to apply.
Familiarity with microscopy sample preparation techniques.
Ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively, willingness to train or teach others, good organizational skills, and openness to working independently as needed.
Some background in computational analysis of microscopy data.
Exposure to correlating images or data from multiple instruments to target a region of interest or support broader sample analysis.
cond_0516.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0516.workplace_support: We aim to support employees across different life and career stages through development resources, workplace flexibility, and inclusive benefits that make it easier to grow, contribute, and stay well.

cond_0611.intro:
